news.title: Russia handed partial international football return as FIFA includes youth team in Under-15 World Cup draw
news.lede: World football’s governing body has taken a significant step toward reintegrating Russia into the international fold after including their youth side in a new tournament. The move marks the first major softening of the stance against the nation since the widespread sporting ban was implemented four years ago. news.title: FIFA Boss Gianni Infantino in Danger of Losing Job? Greek FA President Wants Change at Top
news.lede: FIFA boss Gianni Infantino is hoping to be re-elected in 2027 but may have just received a hard hit as the Greek FA president Makis Gagatsis along with Oliver Bierhoff, who was Germany's team director for 18 years, have called for a change in leadership. Gagatsis confirmed that the GFA does not stand in favour of Infantino's candidacy. The Greek FA pulled its support for the head of FIFA after a proposal of privatisation to raise $20 billion. What They Had to Say"The Greek FA (EPO) has taken a ‌clear position against a candidacy of Gianni Infantino.

news.title: Falconets Receive Huge Warning About Colombia's Credentials At FIFA Women's World Cup
news.lede: Nigeria’s female youth national team, Falconets have received a huge warning that they will not find the going easy when they face Colombia in the quarter-finals of the ongoing FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland, Sports247 reports. The warning comes with a reminder that the South Americans are into the competition’s quarter-finals for a second consecutive edition, though they progressed from Group E of this year’s championship as a third-placed team. With their sudden burst of form turning out to be good enough, Moses Aduku’s squad will have to redouble their efforts in order to overcome the Colombians, who reached the last eight after edging hosts Poland 1-0 on Thursday.

news.title: VAR under scrutiny as technology’s role in football expands
news.lede: Another domestic football season is underway, and already, in mid-September, the shortcomings of technology in sport are at the centre of the discourse once again. The video assistant referee (VAR) is perhaps the most discussed technology in modern sport. While video replays have been in use for years in sports like American football, rugby or cricket, it has only been a decade since the International Football Association Board (IFAB), the highest regulatory authority in the sport, approved the use of VAR. With artificial intelligence (AI) reportedly reaching dangerous levels of development and technological optimisation of people's lives at an all-time high, it is perhaps a pertinent time to consider the use of technology in sport.

news.title: FIFA World Cup 2026 to Feature Expanded Format and Venues
news.lede: The 2026 FIFA World Cup is poised to mark a significant change in the tournament's history, with an expanded format and host locations across three nations: the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The tournament will feature 48 teams, an increase from the traditional 32, which was in place for previous competitions. This adjustment represents FIFA's aim to enhance the global nature of the event, allowing more nations to participate. As a result, the tournament will consist of 80 matches, up from the previous count of 64.

news.title: Great perplexed by Popovic’s ‘strange’ axing of Socceroos skipper
news.lede: Updated September 18, 2026 - 11.31pm. First published at 1.12am. Mark Bosnich cannot understand the “strange” omission of Mat Ryan for the Socceroos after he failed to make the 26-player squad for the side’s upcoming friendlies against Brazil. Tony Popovic named seven uncapped players in his line-up for the games later this month, while 16 members of his impressive World Cup squad were recalled.

news.title: No. 20 Tigers celebrate Memorial Stadium 100th anniversary
news.lede: Mizzou football (2-0, 0-0 SEC) is back at home this week to host Troy (2-0, 0-0 SBC) for the Memorial Stadium 100th anniversary game at 6 p.m. The 20th-ranked team will celebrate the 100th anniversary of Memorial Stadium by wearing special throwback uniforms on the field, according to Mizzou Athletics. The uniforms will bring back Tiger nostalgia, combining elements from several areas of Mizzou football including the 1920's-style "M' on the jersey, 1970's-inspired sleeve stripes and a narrow Block M with a gray facemask reminiscent of the helmet design introduced in 1971, according to Mizzou Athletics. The helmets front bumper will display the six Columns of Francis Quadrangle, while the pants will represent the historic shade of gold worn by the Tigers through the 20th century, according to Mizzou Athletics.
